quotes.text: Honestly, the most rewarding part has been connecting with my fans on such a deep level. Knowing that my music has resonated with so many people and has helped them through tough times is incredibly humbling. I never expected this level of impact, and it's what keeps me going.

I think it's essential to be honest with myself and my emotions when I write songs. Life is filled with ups and downs, and I find it cathartic to express my feelings through music. It's not always easy to be so vulnerable, but I believe that's where the most genuine and relatable art comes from.

Oh, my music has definitely evolved a lot since the beginning. I started at such a young age, and I've been lucky to work with incredible collaborators who have helped me expand my sound. As an artist, I've learned the importance of staying true to myself and not letting anyone else dictate who I should be or what my music should sound like.

For me, music and style go hand in hand. I use fashion as a way to express myself visually, just like I do with my music. It's all about feeling comfortable and empowered in my own skin, and I hope that resonates with my fans too. It's essential to remember that I'm just being myself and that everyone should feel free to do the same.

I'm always working on new music and exploring different sounds. I don't like to limit myself to one specific genre or style, so expect some surprises! I'm also eager to collaborate with other artists and continue pushing my creative boundaries. There's so much I want to achieve, and I'm excited for everyone to join me on this journey.

My advice would be to stay true to yourself and never give up. The music industry can be tough and unpredictable, but if you believe in your talent and work hard, you'll find your path. Don't be afraid to take risks and be vulnerable in your art. Most importantly, cherish your fans and the people who support you—they're the ones who make it all possible.
I used to really not enjoy making music and I still have trouble with it.
I forgot that I started making music because I loved it. And then it became my job so quickly when I was so young that I kind of didn't get to enjoy it as much.
I think that I've come back to enjoying it and that's been really nice.
I was more involved in this album than anything we've made. And I think that came from pure enjoyment. Like, I wanted to.
The greatest thing I've ever learned to do. I'm never not grateful that I do that … all my vocals, and my little synths.
I engineer a lot of my own stuff … and then Finneas comes in and does the rest better than me.
We really didn't even mean to do that, it just came naturally.
There's like a lot of small moments on the album that we didn't really mean to do honestly.
This little breakdown track called 'Over Now'. That was me and Finneas just messing around, making the kind of thing that we were like, 'No one's every going to hear this'.
Finneas [and I] had this realisation: The coolest, bravest thing we could do is just put it out exactly how we made it. It's about 'Do we enjoy this and do we like this?'
I was at the gym all the time in this period. I was doing a lot of cardio.
There weren't a lot of songs that were right for running and jumping rope [to] that I liked enough that had the right BPM [beats per minute].

I found one that I loved so much and remember being like, 'Wow, I wish there was some sort of way I could put this in an AI program and make 800 songs that make me feel the way this song makes me feel'.
It's just fun and dance-y and clubby'.
I got so good at it … I would remix everything [and] I was doing it literally all day, every single day.

I've been starting to go out into the world for the first time since I was young and just biting the bullet and just going outside. Just letting myself be, and trying not to be anxious and terrified the entire time like I have been for years.
I remember just being like, 'I don't know what people want me to make, and I don't know what I'm going to make [or] what people are going to think!' I just was very in my head about it.

Everything is different about it. I've been trying to compare recently, just because I'm getting used to doing it in a different way. And trying to be like, 'It's OK to do that. I'm OK. I'm still able to do that; I'm capable still.'
quotes.publication: Dua Lipa's At Your Service podcast

quotes.text: We were like, 'We've got it all figured out, this is how we're going to do it from now on, and it works really well'. And, you know, touring for a year-and-a-half, then coming back to it, and being way older – and not even much older, but again, the jump between 18 and 21 is a big jump. Just mentally and physically, and realistically. It's just been completely different.

quotes.text: I've gotten a little bit more like, 'OK, it's just change and I'm figuring that out.' It's hard to accept change, it's hard to get over, 'But I did it this way for so long, and it worked so well!' Well, you can't anymore.

quotes.text: When you're a teenager and so much of your career is based around the fact that you're young, and then you get older and people are used to you being young, it's hard for you even. But nobody told me that when you grow up you stop recognising your younger self.
